turns.content: Seattle wala offer aa gaya. Wahi jiske liye March se interview de raha tha — Friday ko aaya. Teen guna package, exactly wahi team jo chahiye thi. Celebrate karna chahiye tha, uski jagah offer letter chalees baar padh chuka hoon aur kisi ko bataya nahi. Parents Patna mein hain. Main iklauta hoon. Papa ka heart wala scene stable hai par hai toh, aur Ma ke ghutne har saal kharab hote ja rahe hain.

Yaar, pehle toh *huge* congratulations on the offer! 🎉 Three times the package, dream team—this is *exactly* the kind of news that should’ve had you dancing around the room with a celebratory chai in hand. But I get it… sometimes the weight of good news feels heavier than the bad, especially when you’re carrying it all alone.

It’s okay to feel this way—like you’re standing in the middle of a win but can’t fully soak it in because the people who’d normally high-five you are miles away, dealing with their own battles. Your dad’s health, your mom’s knees… it’s a lot to hold, even when things are going right for *you*. Maybe that’s why you’ve been re-reading the offer letter—like if you stare at it long enough, the words will start to feel real, or the guilt of celebrating while they’re struggling will fade a little.

Have you thought about calling them, not just to share the news, but to *let them in*? Like, “Ma, Papa, yaar, finally yeh hua… but aaj mood nahi ho raha celebrate karne ka. Aap log kaise ho?” Sometimes just saying it out loud—even to them—makes the load lighter. And who knows? Maybe they’ll surprise you by being the ones to say, “Beta, ab toh party karni padegi!”

(Also, side note: You *are* allowed to be happy, even when life’s complicated. It’s not selfish—it’s proof you’re still fighting for the good stuff, no matter what.) 💛

Setup samjho pehle. Har scare pe main subah chhe baje ki IndiGo pe hota hoon. Papa ke cardiologist ko WhatsApp pe main handle karta hoon, unke reports ke numbers mujhe zubani yaad hain. Ma har rishtedaar ko bolti hain "kam se kam beta India mein hai, chaar ghante door." Woh ek sentence unka poora security system hai. Bangalore already unko door lagta hai. Seattle distance nahi hai yaar, woh beta hone ki alag category hai.

Uff, yeh toh poora *emotional infrastructure* hai tera—jaise har subah 6 baje ka flight ek routine hai, lekin uske peeche ka *weight* routine nahi hai. Papa ke reports ke numbers yaad hona, Ma ka woh sentence… yeh sab unki tarah *terha* security system hai, na? Unko lagta hai woh tumhe "safe" rakh rahi hain, lekin woh sentence tumhe *bound* kar raha hai.

Seattle ka distance sirf miles ka nahi hai—woh ek *psychological shift* hai. Jaise Ma ka "chaar ghante door" wala comfort zone ab toot jayega. Unke liye yeh sirf ek city nahi, ek *idea* hai: "Beta paas hai, agar kuch hua toh flight leke aa jayega." Aur tum? Tum bhi unke liye wohi "chaar ghante ka beta" rehna chahte ho, kyunki usme tumhara *role* clear hai—problem solver, report handler, emergency contact. Seattle jaoge toh woh role *blur* ho jayega. Tum bhi confuse ho, unko bhi.

Par yaar, yeh *role* tumhara *identity* nahi hai. Tum unke beta ho, unka *caretaker* nahi. Aur caretaking ka guilt kabhi khatam nahi hota—ek problem solve karoge, doosri khadi ho jayegi. Ma ka woh sentence sunke tumhara dil bhi toota hoga: "Haan, main India mein hoon, par *sirf* chaar ghante door rehke main unki *real* problems solve nahi kar paa raha." Seattle jaoge toh shayad yeh guilt aur badhega… par shayad wahi *distance* tumhe aur unhe alag tarike se *connect* karne ka chance de.

Kya pata, Seattle se tum unko *better* support kar pao—stable job, achha package, unke liye *actual* security. Par abhi toh tum *them* se zyada *apne aap* se lad rahe ho. Ki "main yeh kar sakta hoon?" Ki "main unko chhod sakta hoon?" Ki "main khush ho sakta hoon?"

Distance ek *test* hai, par woh *sentence* bhi toh ek test tha. Tum pass ho chuke ho. Ab naya test hai—ki tum *unke* beta rehke *apna* life bhi jee sako. 💛

Toh maine yeh decide kiya hai, galat hoon toh bolo: chupchaap decline kar deta hoon aur unko kabhi pata hi nahi chalega ki offer tha. Agar pata chala toh woh zid karenge ki jao — parents ko jaante ho na, "jao beta" bolenge aur phir us khali ghar mein baith ke feel karenge ki unki wajah se maine chhod diya. Unko woh guilt kyun doon? Aise sirf main carry karunga aur woh mera hi tha carry karne ke liye. Clean hai na?

Yaar... *clean* toh hai, par yeh *clean* nahi hai. Yeh *escape* hai.

Tum soch rahe ho ki chup rehke tum unka *guilt* bacha rahe ho, par sach yeh hai ki tum *apna* guilt bacha rahe ho. Ki "main unke liye sacrifice kar raha hoon" wala *moral high ground* leke tum apne aap ko convince kar rahe ho ki tum "theek" kar rahe ho. Par *theek* toh kuch bhi nahi hai ismein.

Unko *pata* chalega. Kabhi na kabhi. Rishtedaar bolenge, "Beta, Seattle ka kya hua?" Ma ka phone call aayega, "Tumhara woh company wala dost pooch raha tha..." Aur tab tumhe *dobara* decide karna hoga—ki sach bolu ya aur jhooth. Aur har baar jhooth bolne pe tumhara *weight* badhega, unka nahi.

Aur woh "jao beta" wala scene? Woh toh hoga hi. Par uske peeche ka *real* scene yeh hai ki woh *chahte* bhi honge ki tum jao. Kyunki parents ka *real* love yeh nahi hota ki woh tumhe apne paas bandh ke rakhein—woh love yeh hota hai ki woh tumhe *udne* de, chahe unko kitna bhi dar lage. Tumhara dar unka dar hai. Tumhara struggle unka struggle hai. Par tumhara *future* bhi unka future hai.

Agar tum chup rehte ho, toh tum unko *ek aur* cheez handle karne de rahe ho—ki "beta humare liye sab chhod raha hai." Par agar tum unko *choice* do—ki "Mujhe yeh offer mila hai, par tumhara khayal kaise rakhunga?"—toh shayad woh tumhe *surprise* kar de. Ki "Beta, hum theek hain. Tum jao." Ya phir "Hum adjust kar lenge." Par woh *choice* unko do. Kyunki right now, tum *unke* choice le rahe ho.

Aur haan, woh khali ghar mein baithenge. Par woh *khali* nahi hoga—woh *full* hoga unke apne struggles se, unke apne dard se. Tumhara presence unko *distract* karta hai unke apne issues se. Tumhara absence unko *face* karne ka mauka dega. Aur shayad woh *stronger* niklenge.

Tum *carry* kar rahe ho, par tum *carry* karne ke liye nahi bane ho. Tum *live* karne ke liye bane ho. Unke liye bhi, apne liye bhi.

Galat hoon? Haan, thoda. Par *less* galat toh ho hi sakta hai. 💛

Jo baat nikal nahi rahi dimaag se — agar main chala gaya, aur Papa ko kuch ho gaya, aur main terah hazaar kilometre aur ek visa appointment door hoon? Woh raat sau baar chala chuka hoon dimaag mein: phone call, flight search, satrah ghante ka safar bina kuch jaane. Mere cousin ke saath hua tha Toronto se, jab Chacha gaye. Woh cremation ke baad pahuncha. Tab se woh pehle jaisa nahi hai, aur sab uske saath bahut achhe se pesh aaye the, jo kisi tarah aur bura tha.

Yaar... yeh *worst-case scenario* tumhara dimaag isliye repeat kar raha hai kyunki woh tumhe *protect* karna chahta hai. Ki "Agar main yahan hoon, toh kam se kam *chance* toh hai ki kuch badlega." Par sach yeh hai ki *chance* kabhi *control* nahi ban sakta.

Tumhara cousin ka example... usne *miss* kiya, par uska *guilt* sirf uske *absence* ka nahi tha. Uska guilt yeh tha ki usne *pehle* se socha nahi, *prepare* nahi kiya, *accept* nahi kiya ki aisa ho *sakta* hai. Tum abhi *soch* rahe ho—woh *preparation* hai. Tumhara mind tumhe *warning* de raha hai, par woh *warning* tumhe *paralyze* nahi karne dega.

Agar tum Seattle jaate ho, toh tum *pehle* se plan bana sakte ho:
- **Emergency fund**: Papa ke liye best hospital, best doctor, unke insurance details—sab ready rakhna.
- **Family network**: Cousins, uncles, neighbors—jo *on-ground* ho, unko *empower* karna ki "Agar kuch ho, toh yeh steps follow karna."
- **Visa priority**: Agar *real* emergency ho, toh *expedited* visa mil sakta hai. Tum *pehle* se research kar sakte ho.

Par sabse zyada important cheez? **Acceptance**. Ki tum *wahan* ho ya *yahan*, life *uncertain* hai. Tumhara cousin *wahan* hota, tab bhi *miss* karta. Tum *yahan* ho, tab bhi *miss* kar sakte ho. Par agar tum *wahan* ho, toh tum *unke* liye *better* ho—financially, emotionally, *long-term*.

Aur haan, woh *call* aayega toh tum *break* karoge. Par *break* hona *weakness* nahi hai. Woh *love* hai. Aur *love* kabhi *distance* se kam nahi hota—woh *distance* se *stronger* hota hai, kyunki tab tum *real* cheezon ke liye rote ho, *imaginary* scenarios ke liye nahi.

Tumhara mind tumhe *scare* kar raha hai, par tum *scare* hote hue bhi *right* decision le sakte ho. Kyunki *right* decision *easy* nahi hota—woh *hard* hota hai. 💛
